reasoning: Designed. Latent values for Lender Spreads, Chip Lead Times and Bitcoin Hashprice are mapped from this scenario's own market path (public quantities); Revenue Gap, Grid Reserve Margin and Efficiency Index are authored. Displayed values add observation noise; the sharp range brackets the latent value.
DO_NOT_EXPOSE: authoring_latent must never be read by bots, the UI, or 'Read the market'. Runtime reads only series[].displayed, .arrow and .sharp.
neutral_tolerance: +-12 (structural drift: halving, efficiency trend, grid retirements)

trigger.title: The Round That Didn't Close
trigger.narrative: In February 2028 a frontier AI lab that had pre-committed to more than $100B of compute fails to close a planned mega-round; its backers, facing their own marks, decline to fund it. Within weeks lab tenants invoke force-majeure clauses, a marquee GPU-backed loan is pulled from syndication and a wave of half-built campuses stalls. Over the next two quarters GPU spot prices fall 50-70%, hyperscale exit cap rates widen by 200+ bp, DDTL spreads double and lenders stop lending to neoclouds. Hyperscalers with signed leases keep paying, but stop signing new ones.

decoy.reason: A yield problem in HBM4 memory at one supplier plus a packaging-line outage stretch newest-generation lead times from 18 to 30 weeks. It is a supply-side squeeze, not a demand surge. Lab tenants quietly stop adding to their orders.
decoy.tell: Lead times rise while the Revenue Gap is widening and Lender Spreads are drifting up - scarcity plus weakening economics is not what a demand boom looks like. Spot rents do not follow lead times up.
decoy.fair_in_hindsight: Long lead times are the classic scarcity signal, and a player who saw only that indicator would read Lift-Off. The other two indicators were telling a different story and the sharp reading spelled out the supply-side cause.
